answer: In a marketplace where AI agents sell ridge maps, reef surveys, and juniper inventories, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities gives an attacker the same voting power as locking them in one account. To gain control, the attacker must acquire and immobilize a majority of the staked tokens, bearing the purchase cost and losing access to that capital while it is locked.
